'''Jan-Michael Peters''' (born 16 August 1962) is a German [[Cell biology|cell]] and [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] whose research focuses on genome organisation and [[chromosome segregation]]. He has been scientific director of the [[Research Institute of Molecular Pathology]] (IMP) in [[Vienna]] since 2013.<ref name="IMP-profile">{{cite web |title=Jan-Michael Peters |url=https://www.imp.ac.at/research/groups/jan-michael-peters |publisher=Research Institute of Molecular Pathology |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Peters was born and grew up in [[Schleswig-Holstein]]. He has described an interest in biology dating back to his childhood.<ref name="Standard-childhood">{{cite news |title=Es kann immer nur einen Entdecker geben |url=http://derstandard.at/1308680334213/Wittgenstein-Preistraeger-Es-kann-immer-nur-einen-Entdecker-geben |work=Der Standard |language=de}}</ref>

Peters began studying biology at the [[University of Kiel]] in 1982, where he received his [[Vordiplom|pre-diploma]]. In 1988, he completed his [[Diplom|diploma]] studies at the [[University of Heidelberg]], where he also obtained his PhD in cell biology in 1991. His doctoral supervisor was [[Werner Franke]].<ref name="IMP-Wittgenstein">{{cite web |title=Jan-Michael Peters receives Wittgenstein Award 2011 |url=https://www.imp.ac.at/fileadmin/content/Communications/News_Items/2011-06-20/110621_Wittgenstein_Peters_E.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201033428/https://www.imp.ac.at/fileadmin/content/Communications/News_Items/2011-06-20/110621_Wittgenstein_Peters_E.pdf |archive-date=1 December 2017 |url-status=unfit |publisher=Research Institute of Molecular Pathology |format=PDF |year=2011}}</ref> His doctoral research included the identification and characterisation of [[Valosin-containing protein|p97 ATPase]] and its relationship to other members of the enzyme family now known as [[AAA proteins|AAA ATPases]],<ref name="p97-1990">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2140770/ PubMed record: PMID 2140770].</ref> as well as the purification and characterisation of the [[Proteasome|26S proteasome]].<ref name="proteasome-1991">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1802724/ PubMed record: PMID 1802724].</ref>

== Career and research ==

=== Career ===
Between 1992 and 1993, Peters worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] with Franke at the [[German Cancer Research Center]] (DKFZ) in [[Heidelberg]], continuing his research on p97 ATPase and the 26S proteasome.<ref name="IMP-Wittgenstein" /><ref name="p97-1992">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1531366/ PubMed record: PMID 1531366].</ref><ref name="proteasome-1993">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8263938/ PubMed record: PMID 8263938].</ref> His work showed that 26S proteasomes are present in both the [[cytoplasm]] and the [[cell nucleus]].<ref name="proteasome-localisation">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8125997/ PubMed record: PMID 8125997].</ref> He also proposed that their 19S regulatory complexes use [[ATP hydrolysis]] to bind and unfold protein substrates and transport them into the proteolytic 20S core.<ref name="proteasome-mechanism">[https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7985232/ PubMed record: PMID 7985232].</ref>

In 1994, Peters joined the laboratory of [[Marc W. Kirschner]] at [[Harvard Medical School]] in [[Boston]] as a postdoctoral fellow, where he contributed to the discovery of the [[Anaphase-promoting complex|anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome]] (APC/C), which regulates chromosome segregation.<ref name="IMP-Wittgenstein" />

Peters joined the IMP in 1996 as a junior group leader and became a senior scientist in 2002. He was appointed scientific deputy director in 2011 and scientific director in 2013, succeeding [[Barry Dickson]].<ref name="IMP-profile" /><ref name="Standard-director">{{cite news |title=Jan-Michael Peters wird neuer wissenschaftlicher Leiter am Wiener IMP |url=http://derstandard.at/1371171162149/Jan-Michael-Peters-wird-neuer-wissenschaftlicher-Leiter-am-Wiener-IMP |work=Der Standard |language=de}}</ref>

=== Chromosome segregation and cell division ===
Peters's research group studies the molecular mechanisms of chromosome organisation, chromosome segregation and [[cell division]].<ref name="IMP-profile" /> His work has examined the regulation and mechanisms of proteins involved in chromosome segregation during [[mitosis]], including APC/C and [[PLK1|polo-like kinase 1]] (PLK1).<ref name="APC-review">{{cite journal |last=Peters |first=J. M. |title=The anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome: a machine designed to destroy |journal=Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology |year=2006 |volume=7 |issue=9 |pages=644–656}}</ref><ref name="PLK1-review">{{cite journal |last1=Petronczki |first1=M. |last2=Lénárt |first2=P. |last3=Peters |first3=J. M. |title=Polo on the Rise—from Mitotic Entry to Cytokinesis with Plk1 |journal=Developmental Cell |year=2008 |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=646–659 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2008.04.014 |pmid=18477449}}</ref> He also contributed to research on PLK1 inhibition as a potential approach to cancer treatment, including a study showing that the inhibitor BI 2536 inhibited tumour growth in preclinical models.<ref name="BI2536">{{cite journal |last1=Steegmaier |first1=M. |last2=Hoffmann |first2=M. |last3=Baum |first3=A. |last4=Lénárt |first4=P. |last5=Petronczki |first5=M. |last6=Krssák |first6=M. |last7=Gürtler |first7=U. |last8=Garin-Chesa |first8=P. |last9=Lieb |first9=S. |last10=Quant |first10=J. |last11=Grauert |first11=M. |last12=Adolf |first12=G. R. |last13=Kraut |first13=N. |last14=Peters |first14=J. M. |last15=Rettig |first15=W. J. |title=BI 2536, a potent and selective inhibitor of polo-like kinase 1, inhibits tumor growth in vivo |journal=Current Biology |year=2007 |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=316–322}}</ref>

=== Genome organisation and cohesin ===
Peters and his colleagues contributed to establishing how [[cohesin]] organises genomic DNA through loop extrusion.<ref name="IMP-profile" /><ref name="IMP-loop-news">{{cite web |title=Cohesin – a molecular motor that folds our genome |url=https://www.imp.ac.at/news/article/cohesin-a-molecular-motor-that-folds-our-genome |publisher=Research Institute of Molecular Pathology |date=21 November 2019 |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref> Their research showed that [[Topologically associating domain|topologically associating domains]] and [[Chromatin|chromatin loops]] depend on cohesin, and that cohesin-associated proteins, including [[WAPL]], [[CTCF]] and PDS5 proteins, regulate the organisation of these structures.<ref name="Wutz-2017">{{cite journal |last1=Wutz |first1=G. |last2=Várnai |first2=C. |last3=Nagasaka |first3=K. |last4=Cisneros |first4=D. A. |last5=Stocsits |first5=R. R. |last6=Tang |first6=W. |last7=Schoenfelder |first7=S. |last8=Jessberger |first8=G. |last9=Muhar |first9=M. |last10=Hossain |first10=M. J. |last11=Walther |first11=N. |last12=Koch |first12=B. |last13=Kueblbeck |first13=M. |last14=Ellenberg |first14=J. |last15=Zuber |first15=J. |last16=Fraser |first16=P. |last17=Peters |first17=J. M. |title=Topologically associating domains and chromatin loops depend on cohesin and are regulated by CTCF, WAPL, and PDS5 proteins |journal=The EMBO Journal |year=2017 |volume=36 |issue=24 |pages=3573–3599 |doi=10.15252/embj.201798004 |pmid=29217591|pmc=5730888 }}</ref> WAPL limits the length and lifetime of loops by promoting cohesin release from chromatin, while CTCF helps determine their genomic positions.<ref name="IMP-profile" />

In 2019, his group used biochemical reconstitution and [[Single-molecule experiment|single-molecule imaging]] to demonstrate that human cohesin, together with [[NIPBL]]–[[MAU2]], acts as an ATP-dependent [[motor protein]] that extrudes DNA into loops.<ref name="Davidson-2019">{{cite journal |last1=Davidson |first1=Iain F. |last2=Bauer |first2=Benedikt |last3=Goetz |first3=Daniela |last4=Tang |first4=Wen |last5=Wutz |first5=Gordana |last6=Peters |first6=Jan-Michael |title=DNA loop extrusion by human cohesin |journal=Science |year=2019 |volume=366 |issue=6471 |pages=1338–1345 |doi=10.1126/science.aaz3418 |pmid=31753851}}</ref>

His group has also investigated the consequences of mutations affecting cohesin and its regulators. A 2022 study showed that several NIPBL mutations associated with [[Cornelia de Lange syndrome]] impair cohesin-mediated DNA loop extrusion, suggesting that defects in this process may contribute to the disorder.<ref name="Panarotto-2022">{{cite journal |last1=Panarotto |first1=Melanie |last2=Davidson |first2=Iain F. |last3=Litos |first3=Gabriele |last4=Schleiffer |first4=Alexander |last5=Peters |first5=Jan-Michael |title=Cornelia de Lange syndrome mutations in NIPBL can impair cohesin-mediated DNA loop extrusion |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=2022 |volume=119 |issue=18 |at=e2201029119 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2201029119 |pmid=35476527 |pmc=9170158}}</ref> His laboratory also studies how cohesin mutations affect genome architecture in cancer.<ref name="IMP-profile" />

=== Collaborative research projects ===
Peters coordinated EuroDYNA, a [[European Science Foundation]] research programme, between 2005 and 2008.<ref name="EuroDYNA-CORDIS">{{cite web |title=EuroDYNA leaves healthy genomic research ecosystem as legacy |url=http://cordis.europa.eu/news/rcn/117536_de |website=CORDIS |publisher=European Commission}}</ref><ref name="EuroDYNA-project">{{cite web |title=EuroDyna project |url=http://www.univie.ac.at/eurodyna/ |publisher=University of Vienna}}</ref> Research associated with the programme included work on the relationship between cohesin and CTCF in [[Regulation of gene expression|gene regulation]].<ref name="EuroDYNA-CORDIS" /> Peters and his colleagues showed that cohesin contributes to CTCF-mediated [[Insulator (genetics)|transcriptional insulation]].<ref name="Wendt-2008">{{cite journal |last1=Wendt |first1=K. S. |last2=Yoshida |first2=K. |last3=Itoh |first3=T. |last4=Bando |first4=M. |last5=Koch |first5=B. |last6=Schirghuber |first6=E. |last7=Tsutsumi |first7=S. |last8=Nagae |first8=G. |last9=Ishihara |first9=K. |last10=Mishiro |first10=T. |last11=Yahata |first11=K. |last12=Imamoto |first12=F. |last13=Aburatani |first13=H. |last14=Nakao |first14=M. |last15=Imamoto |first15=N. |last16=Maeshima |first16=K. |last17=Shirahige |first17=K. |last18=Peters |first18=J. M. |title=Cohesin mediates transcriptional insulation by CCCTC-binding factor |journal=Nature |year=2008 |volume=451 |issue=7180 |pages=796–801 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature06634}}</ref>

Between 2004 and 2009, Peters coordinated the [[Framework_Programmes_for_Research_and_Technological_Development#FP6_and_FP7|European Union-funded]] MitoCheck project, which aimed to identify genes involved in mitosis. Between 2010 and 2015, he headed its successor, MitoSys, an interdisciplinary project investigating how genes and proteins orchestrate mitosis in human cells.<ref name="MitoSys">{{cite web |title=MitoSys: Systems Biology of Mitosis |url=http://www.mitosys.org/ |website=MitoSys}}</ref> MitoSys was accompanied by ''Lens on Life'', an art project and exhibition exploring cell division through collaborations between artists and scientists.<ref name="Lens-IMP">{{cite web |title=Press Release: "Lens on Life" – Artists and Scientists Explore Cell Division |url=https://www.imp.ac.at/news/detail/article/press-release-lens-on-life-artists-and-scientists-explore-cell-divison/?cHash=f4985fb3e8313c9e30ea931d46dbb4b5&L=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201030644/https://www.imp.ac.at/news/detail/article/press-release-lens-on-life-artists-and-scientists-explore-cell-divison/?cHash=f4985fb3e8313c9e30ea931d46dbb4b5&L=0 |archive-date=1 December 2017 |url-status=unfit |publisher=Research Institute of Molecular Pathology}}</ref><ref name="Lens-Artakt">{{cite web |title=Lens On Life – MitoSys – Artakt |url=http://www.artakt.co.uk/projects/mitosys/ |publisher=Artakt}}</ref><ref name="MitoSys-exhibitions">{{cite web |title=Exhibitions – MitoSys: Systems Biology of Mitosis |url=http://www.mitosys.org/exhibitions/ |website=MitoSys}}</ref>
